attest_exemption.notes: A firm with no Kansas office may perform non-attest services for a Kansas client without registering if the work is performed through an individual with practice privileges under K.S.A. 1-322(a). By contrast, any firm without a Kansas office that performs attest services for a Kansas client MUST register -- unconditional trigger. Dual-sourced: statute + KS Board out-of-state firm registration guidance.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with a Kansas office practicing CPA accountancy must register -- unqualified by service type or CPA-title use.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may require peer review as a condition of firm-registration renewal for firms providing attest services, at least once every 3 years; noncompliance is grounds for discipline. Waiver available if no attest services in preceding 12 months.

attest_exemption.notes: Exemption is broader than a non-attest-only carve-out: a no-office firm licensed in good standing at home (and peer-review compliant if applicable) is exempt regardless of attest/non-attest -- so 'false' since attest work by a no-office firm is ALSO exempt, not force-registered.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Qualified trigger: KY office performing attest OR KY office using 'CPA' title triggers licensure -- near-universal in practice since most firms use CPA in their name.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms performing audits/reviews/compilations must enroll in approved peer review; renewal requires proof of current enrollment and most recent report within 3 years.

attest_exemption.notes: Exemption covers attest services too, not just non-attest: a no-office firm can perform attest work without a LA permit if non-CPA owners hold only minority interest, firm is peer-review-enrolled/current, and home-state licensed. Marked false since not restricted to non-attest-only.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Qualified trigger: LA office providing attest services OR using CPA title requires a firm permit.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms providing attest services (excluding PCAOB-permanent-inspection engagements) must enroll in/comply with board-approved peer review; results reportable to board; annual permit renewal.

attest_exemption.notes: Unclear -- section 12253 exempts no-office out-of-state firms meeting substantial-equivalency standards without an explicit attest/non-attest carve-out in the retrieved text. Marked null rather than guess; only the statute itself was confirmed, a board rules PDF could not be parsed.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Qualified trigger: ME office performing attest services (per section 12201(3-A)(A-D)) OR ME office using CPA/CPA-firm title triggers licensure -- narrower than Kansas.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms providing attest services other than compilations must complete approved peer review as a licensure/renewal condition -- initial review within 18 months, then every 3 years. Single-source only.

attest_exemption.citation: Md. Code, Bus. Occ. & Prof. section 2-401
attest_exemption.notes: Broader than the framed question: a no-office firm may perform ATTEST services without a MD permit if it meets peer-review/application requirements (sections 2-402 to 2-403, 2-4A-02) via a practice-privilege individual. Non-attest work under the CPA title likewise exempt via practice-privilege individual. Marked false since attest work is also conditionally exempt, not force-registered.

physical_office_trigger.citation: Md. Code, Bus. Occ. & Prof. section 2-401(a)
physical_office_trigger.notes: Qualified trigger: MD office performing attest services OR MD office using CPA/CPA-firm title requires a permit.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Md. Code, Bus. Occ. & Prof. Title 2, Subtitle 4A; COMAR 09.24.06
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms performing audit/attest engagements must undergo peer review at least every 3 years under an approved program; permit holders certify peer-review status at each renewal. Not required for non-attest-only firms.

attest_exemption.notes: VERIFIED, directive citation confirmed correct. Section 34-1-16's chapeau bars a firm 'with an office in this state' from providing attest services/using CPA title unless registered. Board's own rule (r. 30-X-3-.04, fetched verbatim): 'No firm or office not located in this state...shall be required to register as a firm with this Board.' Nonresident CPAs may render non-attest services without notice/fee (section 34-1-7).

physical_office_trigger.notes: Each office established/maintained in Alabama for public accounting practice must register.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Fetched directly: each Practice Unit must undergo peer review at least every 3rd fiscal year; missing the deadline means the permit 'shall not be renewed for the current fiscal year.'

attest_exemption.notes: No-office firms exempt from the ordinary firm-permit requirement. Attest work for an AK-headquartered client requires a lighter 'out-of-state permit' (notice+fee+verification) rather than a full firm permit; non-attest work needs only quality-review participation, no filing. Split exists but with an intermediate step for attest.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Opening an AK office requires a full firm permit; the no-office exemptions only apply to firms with no AK office.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may require peer review as a condition of firm-permit renewal, not more than once every 3 years. Corroborated by renewal-instructions PDF requiring the most recent peer-review acceptance report attached.

attest_exemption.notes: Broader than the typical split: a no-AZ-office firm may practice, INCLUDING attest, without registration if owned/employing a limited-reciprocity-privilege holder in good standing at home. A.R.S. section 32-731 requires attest/compilation 'only through a registered firm' for firms that fall within the registration net otherwise (AZ office or don't meet the exemption conditions). RESOLVED 2026-08-17: read both sections directly. Section 32-731(A) opens 'Except as provided in section 32-725, subsection G' -- an express statutory carve-out, not an inference. Section 32-731(B)'s second sentence independently confirms it, naming a 32-725(G)-qualified individual as a valid signer for attest/compilation reports. The two sections were never in tension; 32-731 explicitly defers to 32-725(G) by its own text.

physical_office_trigger.notes: No-AZ-office is a mandatory exemption condition; having an AZ office disqualifies the exemption and triggers section 32-730 biennial registration.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Ariz. Admin. Code R4-1-454; A.R.S. section 32-731
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Peer-review results required for new firm applications and reinstatement; less directly confirmed for ordinary biennial renewal specifically.

attest_exemption.notes: No-office firms must register if performing attest services for an AR-headquartered client. No-office firms may provide non-attest services/use CPA title without registering if via practice-privilege individuals + peer-review + home-state licensure compliance. Dual-sourced (statute + independent summary).

physical_office_trigger.notes: AR office practicing public accounting or using CPA/CPA-firm title must register, independent of the no-office attest/non-attest split.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Licensees issuing attest reports must enroll in approved peer review; Rule 20 requires submitting peer-review documents within 30 days of notice or with renewal application, whichever first.

attest_exemption.notes: Out-of-state individual practice-privilege holder may perform non-attest services without CA license/firm registration; may perform an audit/review for a CA-headquartered entity ONLY through a firm registered under section 5096.12. Confirmed independently via CBA's own out-of-state-firm-registrant guidance.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Practice-privilege holder barred from providing services 'from any office located in this state' except as an employee of a CA-registered firm -- opening a CA office forces registration regardless of service type.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: To renew/convert to active registration status, a firm must have a peer review report accepted by a board-recognized program no less than every 3 years -- explicit renewal condition, corroborated by a CBA peer-review overview PDF.

attest_exemption.notes: No-SD-office firm doing non-attest/compilation work via a practice-privileged individual is exempt from a permit; a firm doing attest work (with or without an SD office) for SD clients needs a permit. Net effect matches the framed question.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Office triggers the permit requirement combined with attest services OR restricted CPA/PA title use from that office -- near-universal in practice since almost all firms use the restricted title.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may require peer review by rule as a condition of firm-permit renewal; SD Board's peer review guidance confirms implementation for financial-reporting-scope firms (1 year after starting, every 3 years thereafter).

attest_exemption.notes: A firm must hold a permit to provide attest services or use CPA/PA titling; by negative implication a non-attest, non-titled firm wouldn't need one, but this wasn't confirmed as an explicit stated exemption for out-of-state/no-office firms. Official statute site 403'd; this is inference from secondary excerpts, flagged for future direct verification.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Board grants/renews permits to out-of-state firms that establish a TN office; a firm with multiple locations must obtain a permit for each location.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firm permit renewal applications must disclose the peer review program participated in plus proof of compliance. Secondary source (TN Dept of Commerce Peer Review FAQ) confirms compliance mandatory for renewal.

attest_exemption.notes: Notable outlier: HB 1520 (eff. 2019-09-01) eliminated the firm-license requirement even for ATTEST services by no-Texas-office out-of-state firms, as long as the engagement is via a TX-licensed or practice-privileged individual and the firm submits to TX Board jurisdiction/ownership/peer-review rules. Both attest and non-attest are exempt at the firm level for no-office firms -- the classic split does NOT hold in Texas. Only unconditional trigger is a Texas office.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm must hold a firm license if it establishes or maintains a Texas office -- unconditional, independent of service mix.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: A firm subject to peer review cannot have its office license renewed unless peer review requirements are met. Narrow exemptions for PCAOB-only-inspected firms or SSARS-only firms (must request exemption at renewal).

attest_exemption.citation: Utah Code section 58-26a-305; Utah Admin. Code R156-26a-305
attest_exemption.notes: Exemption is service-neutral, not attest-vs-non-attest based: a no-UT-principal-place-of-business firm meeting home-jurisdiction license/ownership/peer-review requirements is exempt regardless of service type. The operative test is principal-place-of-business location, not service mix. Raw statutory PDF text couldn't be fetched directly; based on secondary (Cornell LII) rendering.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Rule conditions the exemption on principal place of business being outside Utah, not literally 'physical office' -- whether a secondary (non-principal) UT office alone independently triggers registration wasn't confirmed. Marked unclear pending direct statutory text.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Peer review is a condition for license renewal for firms in the practice of public accounting, at least once every 3 years; firms outside scope must notify the Division of exemption at renewal.

attest_exemption.notes: Registration required for a VT-office firm (practicing/using CPA titling), and for a no-office firm performing attest-type services for a VT-home-office client. No-office firm performing non-attest/limited categories for a VT-home-office client is exempt, subject to ownership/practice-privilege conditions. RESOLVED 2026-08-17: independently re-read 26 V.S.A. 74(a)-(b) verbatim at legislature.vermont.gov. Matches the citation exactly: (a)(1)-(2) office-based triggers, (a)(3) the no-office attest trigger for a VT-home-office client, (b) the no-office non-attest exemption. The flagged secondary source (citing a repealed section 78) was never actually used as a citation here -- there is no real disagreement between the sources this record relies on, only a correctly-rejected bad source noted for awareness.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Registration required if the firm has an office established/maintained in Vermont for public accounting practice -- unconditional on specific service mix once a VT office exists.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: 26 V.S.A. section 75; VT Board Admin Rule 10.7
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may require peer review as a renewal condition, no more than every 3 years; Rule 10.7 requires an attestation of peer review within the preceding 3 years in the renewal application. Firms with no attest services aren't required to undergo peer review.

attest_exemption.notes: Statute (per consistent secondary quoting) requires firms to register each MA office and show attest/compilation services are under the charge of a licensed person; separately, out-of-state firms with no MA physical office/principal place of business may provide services without a MA license if maintaining a valid home-state license. Reads as a broader office-based exemption rather than a clean attest/non-attest split. mass.gov/malegislature.gov blocked automated fetch (403/404) for full verbatim confirmation -- marked unclear rather than asserted.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Firms must register each MA office as part of firm permit issuance/renewal -- maintaining an MA office brings the firm into the registration system. Not independently verified against full primary text (fetch blocked), based on consistent secondary quoting.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition for license renewal, practice unit must certify completion of a quality review within the preceding 3 years for audit/attest services; firms issuing no attest/compilation reports are exempt. Confirmed via two independent search passes, primary fetch not directly verified verbatim.

attest_exemption.notes: Does not map to a clean split: a no-MI-office firm can perform review/compilation (subsection 4) AND full attest/other professional services (subsection 5) without a MI license, each 'only if' meeting stated conditions (individual practice privilege, lawful home-state practice, likely peer-review-related conditions). Conditional/gated exemption for attest, not force-registered.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm that establishes/maintains a MI office must obtain a MI license to practice public accounting -- unconditional, service-type-independent. Confirmed via two independent fetches.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Renewal applicant must submit proof of peer review obtained within the preceding 3 years; must enroll with a sponsoring org within 1 year of initial licensure or performing services requiring peer review, report fail/2nd-consecutive-deficiency ratings within 30 days.

attest_exemption.citation: Minn. Stat. section 326A.05, subd. 1(a)(4) and subd. 1(b)-(c)
attest_exemption.notes: Subd 1(a)(4) requires a permit for a no-office firm performing attest for an MN-headquartered client, BUT subd 1(b) exempts a no-office firm with a valid home-state permit from needing an MN permit (including for attest) if the HOME state requires equivalent peer review as a renewal condition and work is via a practice-privileged individual. Attest doesn't unconditionally trigger registration -- gated on home-state peer review regime.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with an MN office performing attest services must hold a permit; MN office also triggers title-registration (CPA/CPA-firm title use) requirements independently.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Permit holders must undergo peer review no more than once every 3 years, in a board-specified manner, as a renewal condition.

attest_exemption.notes: Subsection (a) requires a permit for a no-office firm performing attest/review/compilation for an MS-headquartered client, BUT subsection (b) creates a conditional exemption for such firms 'only if' peer-review-compliant per board rule. Attest/review work by a no-office firm is not unconditionally force-registered -- gated on peer review, same pattern as MN/MO/MI.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with an MS office practicing public accountancy or using CPA/CPA-firm title must hold a permit -- unconditional office-based trigger.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: No-office/review-compilation exemption explicitly conditioned on peer review compliance per board rule; secondary sourcing confirms peer review as a standing renewal condition for attest/compilation firms.

attest_exemption.citation: RSMo section 326.289.1(1)-(3), as re-enacted by HCS SS#2 SB 1233 (2026), effective 2026-08-28
attest_exemption.notes: Read directly from the enacted bill text -- the SAME statute already confirmed as a real event in the reg-change pipeline. A no-MO-office firm MAY offer attest/compilation services WITHOUT a permit if: meets subsection 4(1) qualifications, complies with peer review requirements, works via a practice-privileged individual (section 326.283), and can lawfully do so in the individual's home state. Non-attest/non-compilation services under CPA title without a permit are separately allowed via practice-privileged individual. Missouri does NOT force-register attest work by no-office firms; peer review compliance, not service classification, is the operative gate. A sole-practitioner/single-member-LLC exemption request (new subsection 1(5)) further confirms peer-review status as the real gate.

physical_office_trigger.citation: RSMo section 326.289.1(1)(a)-(b), as enacted by HCS SS#2 SB 1233 (2026)
physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with an MO office offering attest/compilation services, or using CPA/CPA-firm titling, must hold a permit -- effectively universal for MO-office CPA-titled firms.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: RSMo section 326.289.9, as enacted by HCS SS#2 SB 1233 (2026)
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board required by rule to make peer review (no more than once every 3 years) a condition of permit renewal -- carried forward from the pre-08-28 version with minor wording changes ('comparable' replacing 'substantially equivalent'), core peer-review-renewal linkage preserved.

attest_exemption.notes: PR statute defines 'practice of public accounting' narrowly as attest-type services only (Seccion 18(12)) -- explicitly excludes tax prep/consulting/bookkeeping. Firm registration (Seccion 5) is triggered only by that narrow attest definition; non-attest-only firms fall outside the mandatory trigger entirely.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Registration is framed around engaging in PR in the (narrow, attest-only) practice of public accounting, not around office presence. No language makes a bare office an independent trigger.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: License renewal conditions only on CPE evidence from the Colegio de CPA; no peer review mention in the 21-section statute as reviewed. A peer-review mandate could exist in Junta regulations not reached by this research -- not found in the primary law itself.

attest_exemption.notes: A firm needs a Firm Permit to Practice only to provide attest services or use CPA/CPA-firm titling -- UAA-style framework. Non-attest services without the CPA title fall outside the permit requirement.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Applications must list Guam office addresses/CPAs in charge, and establishing a Guam office is described in secondary sources as one route to a permit, but no provision found stating a bare Guam office alone (absent attest/CPA-title use) independently forces registration. Genuinely unclear.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Explicit: Firm Permit renewal requires enrollment in/completion of board-approved peer review for attest-service firms, with a 3-year lookback exemption for firms already reviewed under an equivalent program. Noncompliance is an enforcement ground.

attest_exemption.citation: 27 V.I.C. section 250d(a)(1)(C), (a)(2)-(3) (Public Accountancy Act of 2014, Act No. 7596)
attest_exemption.notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-17: extracted and read the board's own compiled Act 7596 PDF directly (via curl + pypdf; WebFetch alone exceeded its download size limit on this file). Found the real section -- 250d, not 250e (250e is genuinely 'Appointment of a Resident Agent,' confirming the 2019 Justia archive was correct all along; the two search-derived syntheses that pointed at 250e were simply wrong about the number, though right about the substance). Section 250d(a)(1)(C): a no-VI-office firm performing attest services for a VI-home-office client MUST hold a permit -- no office-based exemption for attest. Section 250d(a)(2)-(3): a no-office firm may perform OTHER (non-attest) services via a practice-privileged individual without a firm permit. Same UAA-model shape as most other states in this dataset.

physical_office_trigger.notes: FILLED 2026-08-17 (previously no source located): section 250d(a)(1)(A)-(B) requires a permit for 'any firm with an office in the Territory performing attest services' or 'with an office... that uses the title CPA or CPA firm' -- office presence alone is not an independent trigger, it's always paired with attest work or CPA-title use, matching the majority pattern in this dataset.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: CONFIRMED 2026-08-17 at the correct citation (250d(h), not 250e): as a condition of permit renewal, applicants must undergo peer review no more than once every 3 years, verifying that individuals supervising attest/compilation services meet professional-standards competency requirements. Directly read, not inferred from a search synthesis.

attest_exemption.citation: CNMI Public Law 13-52 (Accountancy Act of 2002), Section 13(a) with Section 7(a)
attest_exemption.notes: Full primary text read directly. Section 7(a) requires a permit to practice public accountancy (broadly defined to include non-attest per Section 3(g)), but Section 13(a)'s operative prohibition only bars issuing a report on financial statements without a permit, and explicitly does NOT prohibit non-attest services (tax returns, management advisory, financial statement prep without report issuance). Net effect: non-attest services are lawful without a CNMI firm permit; only report/attest issuance is gated. Synthesis of two interacting provisions, flagged as such.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Requires a permitted firm to register each CNMI office -- a sub-requirement of firms already needing a permit, not an independent standalone trigger. This 2002-vintage Act lacks any UAA-style no-notice mobility/practice-privilege provision, unlike Guam/DC/USVI's more modern statutes.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Statute only AUTHORIZES the Board to require peer review as a renewal condition by rule -- not self-executing. Whether the CNMI Board has actually adopted such a rule could not be confirmed; this fleet's prior research found the CNMI Board has minimal-to-no public web presence and per NASBA is not currently accepting CPA exam applications.

attest_exemption.notes: CONFIRMS the directive's original lead against the actual OAB statutes/rules PDF. Registration required only for: OK-office+practice/attest (1), OK-office+CPA/PA titling (2), or no-office+attest for an OK client (3, with its own mobility carve-out via 15.12A/15.30). A no-office firm doing ONLY non-attest work is captured by no trigger. Section 15.15C states the safe harbor explicitly.

physical_office_trigger.notes: OK office triggers registration via practice-of-public-accounting/attest OR CPA/PA titling; practice of public accounting is defined broadly (includes bookkeeping/tax/advisory), so nearly any active OK office triggers registration in practice.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may require peer review (not less than every 3 years) as a condition for permit issuance/renewal for attest-performing applicants; also a mandatory element of the no-office attest-mobility exemption.

attest_exemption.notes: No-OR-office firm may perform non-attest services under CPA title without registering via an authorized practitioner (essentially unconditioned); may also perform attest/compilation without registering but under stricter conditions (qualifications + authorized practitioner).

physical_office_trigger.notes: Confirmed verbatim: registration required only if a business organization has an OR office AND (uses CPA title OR performs attest/compilation) -- the 'and' means office alone doesn't independently trigger registration.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms must certify most recent peer review result on initial, reinstatement, and every renewal application; attest/review/compilation firms must enroll in Peer Review.

attest_exemption.notes: PA does NOT gate on attest-vs-non-attest for no-office firms: the 'qualified unlicensed entity' mobility exemption (section 5.4) requires only no PA office + lawful home-state practice + individual practice-privilege/licensee performing the work -- NOT limited to non-attest work. The only attest-specific rule requires the individual in charge to be a real licensed CPA/PA, not that the firm itself get licensed. PA's gate is individual qualification, not firm-level service classification. RESOLVED 2026-08-17: independently read 63 P.S. 5.4 verbatim (extracted the board's own compiled CPA Law PDF directly). Confirmed word for word: the 'qualified unlicensed entity' exemption (5.4(b)-(d)) tests only (1) no PA office and (2) the individual performing the work being properly qualified under 5.2 or as a licensee -- no attest/non-attest distinction appears anywhere in section 5.4. This was always a correctly-sourced structural fact, not an unresolved disagreement between competing sources; the flag was really a product-design note (PA's model differs from OK/OR/SC's) that doesn't belong in a field meant to force a NOT_VERIFIED withhold.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Mobility exemption (qualified unlicensed entity) requires NO PA office; a firm with ANY PA office cannot use it and must be a licensed qualified association regardless of services performed -- unconditional office trigger, cleaner than OK/OR/SC's office+activity formulations.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition for firm renewal license (or initial license for a firm previously practicing elsewhere), board requires peer review unless exempted. Dual-sourced via 49 Pa. Code 11.82(a).

attest_exemption.notes: Practice unit must hold a permit to provide attest/compilation services or use CPA/CPA-firm titling. Trigger is framed around service-type/title-use rather than explicitly 'no office,' but practical result for an out-of-state no-office firm matches the framed question.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Confirmed directly: maintaining a physical RI office alone does not trigger the permit requirement -- trigger is service type/title use. A firm that DOES need a permit must then register each RI office.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board requires peer review (not more than once every 3 years) as a condition to permit renewal. Dual-sourced across Justia and direct statute citation.

attest_exemption.notes: No-SC-office firm must register only if performing attest/compilation for an SC client, unless exempt under 40-2-30(I)'s practice-privilege pathway. No-office firm doing ONLY non-attest services isn't captured by any part of section 40-2-40(B), no registration needed.

physical_office_trigger.notes: SC-office firm must register if performing attest/practice of accounting OR using CPA/CPA-firm titling. 'Practice of accounting' broadly defined -- essentially any active SC office triggers registration in practice.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a renewal condition, an applicant engaging in attest/compilation must provide evidence of satisfactory peer review no more than once every 3 years.

attest_exemption.notes: Firm-licensing statute is scoped only to attest/compilation/financial-statement-prep services (subsection A); non-attest services fall outside the statute entirely regardless of office. Subsection C lets a firm with principal place of business elsewhere provide those same services without a VA license if home-state licensed and practice-privilege conditions (section 54.1-4411) are met -- this is the SAME statute already confirmed as a real event in the reg-change pipeline.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Licensure turns on principal place of business in VA combined with attest/compilation/financial-statement-prep services -- not mere office presence, not independent of services performed.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms in the AICPA/board-approved practice-monitoring program scope shall enroll. VA Board's own firm-renewal page independently confirms renewal requires peer-review compliance affirmation.

attest_exemption.notes: No-WA-office firm may perform compilation/non-attest services under CPA title without a license only via a practice-privileged individual; attest services subject to separate licensing/mobility conditions.

physical_office_trigger.notes: License required for a WA-office firm performing/offering attest or compilation services -- office is coupled to service type, not independent.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms offering/performing attest services must participate in a board-approved peer review program as a condition of renewing each firm license; documentation due by April 30 of renewal year.

attest_exemption.citation: W. Va. Code section 30-9-17(d); section 30-9-16(f)-(g) (mobility attest carve-out)
attest_exemption.notes: A no-WV-office firm not performing attest/compilation for a WV-home-office client may perform other professional services using the CPA/CPA-firm title without a permit, via a practice-privileged individual. RESOLVED 2026-08-17: read section 30-9-16 (the mobility section itself) directly. For WV-home-office attest work specifically, subsection (f) requires it be performed through a firm holding BOTH a section 30-9-17 permit AND a section 30-9-19 authorization -- but subsection (g) carves out an individual substantial-equivalency practitioner: that individual may perform the same (f) attest services WITHOUT the 30-9-17 firm permit, but MUST still obtain the 30-9-19 authorization. So mobility grants relief from the permit specifically for a lone individual practitioner, never from the authorization, and never for a firm as such -- the two credentials are not granted or withheld together.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A WV-office firm performing attest/compilation, or using CPA/CPA-firm titling, must hold a permit -- the title-use clause makes an in-state office an independent trigger regardless of specific services once titling is used.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Peer review compliance is a condition of a SEPARATE firm 'authorization' (section 30-9-19) needed to sign attest/compilation reports, distinct from the base firm 'permit' (section 30-9-17) whose own renewal provision doesn't list peer review. CONFIRMED 2026-08-17 directly from section 30-9-16(g): the mobility section itself names the 30-9-19 authorization (not the 30-9-17 permit) as what an individual practitioner must obtain for WV-home-office attest work -- independent confirmation that peer review (a condition of the authorization) binds mobility-privileged individuals performing attest work, not just firms with a permit.

attest_exemption.notes: Section 442.025 exempts non-attest services (management advisory, tax prep, financial statement prep without report issuance) from any ch. 442 license requirement; firm licensure under 442.08 ties to attest services being under the charge of a WI-licensed individual. Inferred by cross-referencing two sections, not one dispositive sentence -- WI has no single explicit 'no Wisconsin office' clause like WV/WY/VA/WA.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Unclear/conflicting: section 442.02(1m)(b) lists office maintenance as one way a firm is deemed 'in practice,' suggesting office alone could trigger licensure, but 442.025(6)-(7)'s non-attest exemption appears to override this for firms doing no attest/report work regardless of office. No agency guidance/case law found resolving the interaction.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Department may not renew a firm's license unless, at least once every 3 years, the firm undergoes peer review -- explicit statutory renewal condition, directly quoted.

attest_exemption.notes: Not limited to non-attest work: a no-WY-office firm may perform ATTEST or compilation services for a WY-home-office client and use CPA titling WITHOUT a permit if it meets ownership/peer-review qualifications (33-3-132) via a practice-privileged individual (33-3-116(a)); (xv) separately covers non-attest similarly. Wyoming gates attest work on peer-review/practice-privilege compliance rather than requiring a full firm permit. Confirmed via full verbatim statute text.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A WY-office firm performing attest/compensated public accounting services, OR using CPA/CPA-firm titling, must hold a permit -- the title clause makes an in-state office an independent trigger whenever CPA titling is used.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Failure to show compliance with practice-monitoring (peer review) programs is grounds for the board to revoke/refuse-to-renew a permit -- structured as disciplinary ground rather than a checklist item. Corroborated by cpaboard.wyo.gov's peer-review page (3.5-year review cycles).

attest_exemption.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. section 466-7(d); section 466-3; Haw. Admin. Rules section 16-71-24(b)
attest_exemption.notes: No attest-specific carve-out: ALL firms engaged in the (broadly-defined, includes non-attest) practice of public accountancy in Hawaii must hold a firm permit, even with no permanent HI office (they need only designate one principal holding a current HI individual permit). No statutory split exempting non-attest-only out-of-state firms; Hawaii has no firm-level enhanced-mobility statute comparable to IL/IA.

physical_office_trigger.citation: Haw. Admin. Rules section 16-71-24(b)(3)-(4); Haw. Rev. Stat. section 466-7(d)
physical_office_trigger.notes: Not independent in the sense asked -- the firm-permit duty already attaches to ANY firm engaged in HI public accounting regardless of office. A physical HI office changes STRINGENCY (all principals of an office-having firm must individually hold permits, vs. just one principal for a no-office firm), not whether registration is required at all.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. section 466-7(b)(5); section 466-34(a); section 466-39
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Directly confirmed: permit renewal requires proof of peer review; every permitted firm must undergo peer review every 3 years; a fail/pass-with-deficiency rating may result in denial/termination/nonrenewal of the permit.

attest_exemption.notes: Registration trigger is framed around attest/compilation services or restricted CPA/LPA titling, not physical presence. A no-office firm doing only non-attest work without a CPA-style name isn't required to register. Attest/compilation work must run through a firm registered in Idaho or an equivalent other-state law.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Registration requirement ties to performing attest/compilation or using restricted titles, not office presence per se; office-establishment language in the statute is procedural/administrative, not an independent substantive trigger.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition of registration renewal, board by rule requires firms to comply with peer review requirements. Confirmed via official Idaho Legislature page but through an AI-summarized fetch rather than verbatim capture -- flagged for a currency check against IDAPA 24.30.01 before shipping.

attest_exemption.notes: No-IL-office firm exempt from licensure for non-attest work via practice-privilege individuals. More permissive than a strict binary: under 'enhanced mobility' (450/5.2(a-5)), a no-office firm can ALSO perform attest work for IL-headquartered clients without a license if peer-review/qualification conditions (450/14.4, 450/16) are met -- license required only if those enhanced-mobility conditions aren't met.

physical_office_trigger.notes: IL office alone isn't unconditional: license required if IL office AND (CPA/CPA-firm titling OR the office performs 'accountancy activities' per 8.05(a)(1), the attest/assurance category specifically). An IL office doing only non-attest work under a non-CPA name wouldn't trigger licensure on plain text.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition for renewal license for CPA firms/sole practitioners performing accountancy activities under 8.05(a)(1), department requires satisfactory peer review completion during the preceding 3-year period. Confirmed verbatim against official IL General Assembly text.

attest_exemption.notes: DIRECTIVE'S CITATION CONFIRMED ACCURATE against current codification, cross-checked with Justia historical text (dual-sourced). A no-IN-office firm doing only non-attest work (no attest reports, no CPA title) needs no permit; attest work, report issuance, or CPA title use requires one.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Office registration is a duty on firms that already must hold/apply for a permit -- the underlying obligation to hold a permit at all comes from the attest/CPA-title trigger, not office presence itself. No provision makes an IN office independently trigger it.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: DIRECTIVE'S CITATIONS CONFIRMED ACCURATE. Board must adopt rules requiring peer review (not more than once every 3 years) as a condition to renew a permit; 872 IAC 1-6-9 makes enrollment a renewal condition for attest/compilation-report firms, with a narrow carve-out for firms doing only financial-statement-prep.

attest_exemption.notes: No-office, non-CPA-titled firm exempt from a permit for any service. More permissive than a strict binary: current Iowa Code section 542.20(6)(c) lets an individual practice-privilege holder provide ATTEST services through an out-of-state firm (validly licensed at home, ownership/peer-review compliant) without that firm needing an Iowa permit. Note: an older admin rule (193A-13.4(2), 2017 text) reads narrower (limits to 'review' services) -- current Code text is broader per a 2017 amendment; flagged for a currency check on the rule text.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Permit required only if IA office AND use of a restricted CPA-style title -- office alone is insufficient on the statute's plain terms.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Iowa Code section 542.7(8)(a); Iowa Admin. Code 193A-13.4(3)
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board by rule requires peer review as a condition of firm-permit renewal, confirmed verbatim in both the Iowa Code and implementing admin rule (at least once every 3 years).

attest_exemption.notes: No-office firm avoids a firm permit for BOTH attest (subsection C) and non-attest (subsection D) work via practice-privilege individuals -- attest carries an extra peer-review condition (subsection L/(H)(1)) but isn't an independent registration trigger, just a heavier-condition version of the same exemption. Cross-checked against a second source.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Statute conditions the office trigger on attest work or CPA/CPA-firm title use; NM Board's FAQ states plainly a permit is required for any NM office -- functionally the same result in practice. RESOLVED 2026-08-17: independently re-read NMSA 61-28B-13(B) verbatim -- confirms the statute's own trigger is precisely conditioned on attest work or CPA/CPA-firm title use, never bare office presence alone. The Board's FAQ is informal, non-binding guidance, not an adopted rule -- it has no authority to override the statute's own text, so this was never a true legal conflict between two binding sources (unlike, for example, a statute-vs-formally-adopted-rule disagreement). The FAQ's looser phrasing is an oversimplification worth knowing about, not a competing legal answer.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: NMSA 1978 section 61-28B-13(L); NMAC Title 16, Ch. 60, Part 4
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition to permit renewal, applicant must undergo peer review per board rules. Confirmed by NMAC 16.60.4.

attest_exemption.notes: Firm registration required if engaging in attest/compilation practice or using CPA/PA in its name; a firm limited to non-attest services may register but isn't required to. Confirmed by NYSED's own guidance pages. RESOLVED 2026-08-17: independently re-read NY Education Law 7408(3)(a) verbatim -- 'Any firm... uses the title "CPA" or "CPA firm"... must register with the department,' with no office-presence qualifier anywhere in that clause. Confirms the earlier conclusion directly rather than just citing NYSED guidance a second time: the search-summary claim that a CPA-titled no-office firm could skip registration was simply incorrect, not a competing legitimate reading of a real primary source.

physical_office_trigger.citation: NY Education Law section 7408(3); 8 NYCRR section 70.8(d)
physical_office_trigger.notes: Trigger is attest/compilation practice or CPA/PA title use; office count is only a fee variable ($50/office) and disclosure item, not an independent trigger. Confirmed by NYSED guidance.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: NY Education Law section 7410(1); 8 NYCRR section 70.10
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Peer review required as a condition to renewal of firm registration. Non-participating firms file an annual non-participation notice instead.

attest_exemption.notes: No-NC-office firm may perform non-attest services without registering; must file a no-fee Notice of Intent to Practice only if a practice-privilege individual performs an audit/SAS engagement, SSAE examination, or PCAOB-standard engagement. Dual-sourced via NC Board's own mobility page.

physical_office_trigger.notes: No-permit mobility exemption applies only to a firm with no NC principal place of business/office; NC Board guidance confirms any NC office removes exemption eligibility.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firm desiring to obtain/maintain registration must offer satisfactory evidence of peer review compliance. Reviews valid a minimum of 3 years, subject to board-ordered remedial action.

attest_exemption.notes: Exemption is not conditioned on attest vs non-attest: a no-office firm may perform any practice-of-public-accountancy service, including attest, without a firm permit via a practice-privileged individual. No separate attest-triggered notice/registration requirement -- office location, not service type, is the trigger. Read directly from the official statute text.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with an ND office practicing public accountancy or using CPA/LPA titling must hold a permit. Confirmed by ND Board's own Firms page.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board has permissive authority to require practice reviews (not more than once every 3 years) as a renewal condition; ND Board's site confirms this is implemented for firms performing attest services.

attest_exemption.citation: Ohio Rev. Code section 4701.04(A); section 4701.14; Ohio Admin. Code 4701-13-02
attest_exemption.notes: Statute requires registration only for a firm 'located in this state,' with no explicit attest carve-out for no-office firms, but OAC 4701-13-02 separately requires any firm issuing attest reports to notify/register as a peer review firm within 90 days without clearly limiting that duty to Ohio-located firms. Could not resolve the tension from primary text alone -- marked unclear rather than guessed. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-17: independently re-read both texts at codes.ohio.gov (both current, statute amended eff. 2025-09-30, rule eff. 2025-09-01). Confirmed the tension is real, not resolvable with certainty from primary text alone: OAC 4701-13-02(C) requires 'any' attest-performing firm to 'register with the board as a peer review firm pursuant to section 4701.04,' with no explicit location qualifier in (C)/(D)/(E) themselves. One plausible reading: 'pursuant to section 4701.04' imports that section's own location-scoped registration mechanism, so a no-Ohio-office firm has nothing to register into. An equally plausible reading: (C) creates an independent trigger and 'pursuant to section 4701.04' means only 'via that section's process,' not its scope. Genuinely unresolved either way -- flagging both readings for whoever picks this up next rather than picking one without a textual tiebreaker.

physical_office_trigger.notes: No public accounting firm located in Ohio may practice without registering; practice of public accounting is defined broadly (includes attest and, by board rule, other accounting-skill services for CPA-affiliated firms).

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Ohio Rev. Code section 4701.04(F); Ohio Admin. Code 4701-13-02
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: As a condition for initial/renewal registration, the board requires peer review by rule unless an exception in division (J) applies. OAC 4701-13-02 requires documentation of approved peer review by the October 31 renewal deadline.

ohio.source_disagreement: Statute ties firm registration to being located in Ohio (implying no attest-specific trigger for no-office firms), but OAC 4701-13-02's 90-day notify-and-register duty for attest reports isn't clearly scoped to location -- unresolved tension drove the unclear call.

attest_exemption.notes: No-MT-office firm exempt from registration for BOTH attest and non-attest work; attest doesn't independently force registration. No-office firms doing attest/compilation must satisfy substantive conditions instead (peer review, ownership quals, practice-privilege individual, home-state licensure). Dual-sourced: statute + Board FAQ.

physical_office_trigger.notes: All firms establishing/maintaining an MT office for public accounting practice must register annually -- unconditional, service-agnostic. Dual-sourced: statute + Board Mobility page.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Registered firms performing attest engagements must enroll in peer review; noncompliance/failing reports are disciplinable, threatening registration -- enforcement-based rather than explicit renewal-denial clause. Single-source.

attest_exemption.citation: 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 11, section 005.01; ch. 3, section 001; Neb. Rev. Stat. section 1-125.01(4)
attest_exemption.notes: Admin rule + Board guidance require firm registration for ANY public accounting work for an NE client, attest or not -- no clean no-office/non-attest exemption. Caveat: firm-registration statute is permissive ('may register') and individual-mobility statute ties routing-through-a-permitted-firm specifically to attestation, creating internal tension with the stricter rule/guidance (resolved in favor of the rule). CITATION CORRECTED 2026-08-17: the individual-mobility statute is section 1-125.01, not 1-126 (1-126 is unrelated -- optional partnership/LLC registration mechanics). Read 1-125.01(4) directly: 'Any person who exercises the practice privilege afforded under this section and who, for any entity with its home office in this state, performs attestation services, may only do so through a firm or an affiliated entity which holds a permit issued under section 1-136.' This conditions firm-permit routing on attestation specifically and is silent on non-attest work -- it doesn't affirmatively exempt non-attest work from all registration, but its silence is genuinely readable either way. Unlike Arizona (which had an express 'except as provided in' cross-reference), nothing in 1-125.01 or the admin rule itself resolves the silence one way or the other. Confirmed still current: statute effective 2026-07-18 (LB718), before this record's own last verification, so no post-verification drift.

physical_office_trigger.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. section 1-135; 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 10, section 001
physical_office_trigger.notes: Each office established/maintained in NE for public accountancy practice must be registered annually, independent of services performed. Dual-sourced: statute + near-identical implementing rule.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. section 1-153; 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 13, section 004.01/.03(B)
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board may restrict permits based on peer review results; attest/compilation firms must furnish peer review evidence with renewal application; preparation-only firms exempt. Dual-sourced.

nebraska.source_disagreement: Attest-exemption question only: the individual-mobility statute (Neb. Rev. Stat. 1-125.01(4)) conditions firm-permit routing on attestation specifically and is silent on non-attest work; the administrative rule (288 NAC ch. 11 section 005.01) requires registration for ANY public accounting work, attest or not, with no such carve-out. Genuinely unresolved by the statute's own text -- the stricter administrative rule is used as the primary answer, a conservative reading, not a forced resolution of the tension.

attest_exemption.notes: Full firm-mobility state: an out-of-state firm in good standing at home is deemed a NV CPA firm 'for all purposes' and exempt from registration, no carve-out reinstating the duty for attest work. Only condition is no NV office. The classic attest/non-attest split does not hold in Nevada. Dual-sourced: statute + Board's Out-of-State-Information guidance.

physical_office_trigger.notes: A firm with an NV office must register if it performs attest/compilation, practices public accounting, or uses the CPA designation -- office presence removes the mobility exemption, then combines with any of those triggers. Dual-sourced: NRS text + NAC 628.010(3)(c).

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Renewal provisions condition renewal only on fee payment and CE -- none reference peer review. Peer review is a separate mandatory-enrollment duty enforced through discipline for noncompliance, not framed as a renewal precondition. Triple-sourced (three independent renewal provisions all omit peer review).

attest_exemption.notes: No-office firm doing non-attest services under CPA title doesn't need a permit via practice-privileged individuals; no-office firm doing attest for an NH-home-office client generally needs a permit unless it separately qualifies for a narrow mobility exemption (ownership/experience quals, practice-privilege individuals only, home-state licensure). Second source (Ac 302.05(a)-(b)) confirms the permit requirement ties to assurance/compilation for NH-home-office clients. RESOLVED 2026-08-17: independently read the current adopted text at gc.nh.gov (Document #14399, eff 12-5-25) directly, not a secondary mirror -- confirms Ac 302.05 is titled "CPA Firm Permit Requirements" post-renumbering (formerly Ac 301.10) and subsection (b) reads verbatim: "Each CPA firm seeking a permit to practice as a CPA firm in NH that provides assurance services or compilation services for a client having its home office in NH shall..." -- exact match to this citation's use.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Office-holding firm using CPA/CPA-firm designation needs a permit regardless of service mix; office-holding firms doing attest/compilation also need one. De facto independent trigger for essentially any NH-office accounting firm. RESOLVED 2026-08-17: Ac 303.05 is titled "CPA Firms" post-renumbering (formerly Ac 302.07), subsection (c) reads verbatim: "The applicant CPA firm shall demonstrate, pursuant to RSA 309-B:8, I, that it has or will have a physical presence in NH by a date certain..." -- exact match, confirmed against the state's own current text.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board shall require peer review as a condition to renewal of permits; rule requires a signed Peer Review Affidavit with each application/renewal, issuing only a time-limited conditional permit if the most recent review was adverse/qualified. Dual-sourced, unusually explicit. RESOLVED 2026-08-17: confirmed directly -- Ac 302.07 ("Affidavit for Peer Review") and Ac 303.05(g)-(i) (peer-review-affidavit compliance, conditional permit on an adverse/qualified report) both read exactly as this citation describes under the current (Document #14399, eff 12-5-25) numbering.

attest_exemption.notes: Registration required only if NJ office + attest work, NJ office + CPA titling, or (no NJ office) offering attest services to NJ clients -- unless narrow practice-privilege conditions are met. No-office firm doing only non-attest work may operate unregistered via practice-privileged individuals. Dual-sourced: statute + implementing rule, agreeing.

physical_office_trigger.notes: NJ office alone isn't independent: registration required only if the NJ office does attest work OR uses CPA/Certified-Public-Accountant titling there. A bare NJ office doing only non-attest work under a non-CPA name wouldn't be forced to register on the statutory text.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Triennial registration application must include peer review compliance forms; Peer Review Program participation mandatory for attest/accounting-and-auditing firms (report-free-compilation-only firms exempt). No explicit 'shall refuse to renew' clause found -- inferred from application-bundling + mandatory-participation rules rather than one unambiguous sentence. RESOLVED 2026-08-17: read 45:2B-59 verbatim at law.justia.com. Two DIFFERENT peer-review mechanisms exist in NJ law, not one in tension with itself: (c)(1) lets the board order a peer review as a discretionary REMEDY/SANCTION in a disciplinary proceeding ('in lieu of or in addition to' other discipline) -- that's a case-specific tool, not the standing requirement. Separately and independently, (a)(3) lets the board refuse to renew a registration for 'failure... to maintain compliance with the requirements for issuance or renewal' -- a general ground that reaches the STANDING peer-review-program participation mandate in 13:29-5.4(a), since that's one of the requirements for renewal. The two subsections describe different things; neither undermines the other. Peer review compliance is a real renewal gate via (a)(3), not merely remedial via (c)(1).

attest_exemption.notes: Inferred by combining the unlawful-acts list (unregistered attest/audit prohibited) with the firm-mobility exemption (non-attest CO work 'incident to' out-of-state practice doesn't require registration) -- not one explicit sentence. Board FAQ blocked (403), statute-only.

physical_office_trigger.citation: C.R.S. section 12-100-114 with section 12-100-117(2)(a)(II); 3 CCR 705-1 Rule 1.15(C)(1)(a)
physical_office_trigger.notes: Inferred: a standing CO office isn't 'incidental' to out-of-state practice, falls outside the exemption, triggers resident-manager/registration obligations. Single source, Board FAQ blocked.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board cannot renew registration for a firm issuing attest/compilation reports unless it has attested to peer review. Board's live PeerReview page 403'd, corroborated via cache only.

attest_exemption.notes: No-CT-office firm doing attest work for a CT-headquartered client needs a permit; no-office firm doing only non-attest work may use CPA titling without a permit if quality-review-qualified and working via a practice-privilege individual. Dual-sourced: statute + portal.ct.gov firm-permit page.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Permit required for CT office + attest work, or CT office + CPA titling -- near-universal trigger in practice since most firms use CPA titling. Dual-sourced.

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Quality review every 3 years as a condition of permit renewal; annual waiver available for firms attesting no attest/financial-reporting work. Dual-sourced.

attest_exemption.citation: 24 Del. C. sections 109(c), 111(b); 24 Del. Admin. Code 100 section 10.1
attest_exemption.notes: Broader than the framed split: a no-DE-office firm practicing through a practice-privileged individual has no firm-permit obligation at all, drawing no attest/non-attest line and no 'client home office in DE' carve-out. Attest work via a practice-privileged individual is ALSO exempt -- marked false since DE doesn't force registration specifically for attest work. Dual-sourced: statute + admin code, verbatim agreement.

physical_office_trigger.citation: 24 Del. C. section 111(a); 24 Del. Admin. Code 100 sections 10.2, 10.3
physical_office_trigger.notes: Any firm with a DE office engaged in public accounting practice must obtain/maintain a permit -- unconditional on service type. Dual-sourced, statute + rule verbatim agreement.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: 24 Del. C. section 111(m); 24 Del. Admin. Code 100 sections 10.4, 10.6, 10.12.2.1-3
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Board-approved peer review enrollment required as a condition of permit renewal for attest/compilation firms (eff. 2017-07-01); also a condition of initial issuance. Firms doing only SSARS prep (no attest/compilation) exempt from enrollment. Dual-sourced.

attest_exemption.notes: No-DC-office firm may perform non-attest services without registering via a practice-privileged individual; same no-office firm MUST register for attest services for a DC-headquartered client. Directly on point, unambiguous.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Not truly independent: registration required for a DC-office firm only when it also performs attest services or uses CPA/CPA-firm titling. No requirement for a DC-office firm doing only non-attest work under a non-CPA name.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: 17 DCMR section 2548; renewal mechanics at 17 DCMR section 2547
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms performing audits/reviews/compilations/SSAE-SAS-SSARS engagements must enroll in/complete board-approved peer review. Direct 'condition of renewal' cross-reference in section 2547 not found verbatim in the excerpt retrieved -- inferred from the regulatory scheme.

attest_exemption.citation: Fla. Stat. section 473.3101(1)(a)-(c), with section 473.3141(4) and section 473.302(8)(a)
attest_exemption.notes: Licensure required only if: FL office + attest/CPA titling, OR no FL office + attest work for a FL-headquartered client (with a no-notice mobility pathway if 473.309-qualified + peer-review enrolled). No-office firms doing only non-attest work aren't addressed at all -- no trigger. Dual-sourced: statute + DBPR Mobility FAQ.

physical_office_trigger.notes: Strictly FL office + (attest OR CPA titling), but near-universal in practice since nearly all firms use CPA titling. Dual-sourced: statute + DBPR Mobility FAQ, no service-type carve-out for an FL office.

peer_review_conditions_permit.citation: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-39.005(2)-(3)(a); Fla. Stat. section 473.3125(4)
peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms performing 473.3125(4)-covered services must enroll in board-approved peer review prior to renewal or initial licensure. Dual-sourced: statute + admin rule.

attest_exemption.notes: Actual line is 3-way not binary: audit/SAS/SSAE/PCAOB attest never exempt for no-office firms; compilation/review conditionally exempt with peer-review enrollment; other non-attest fully exempt via a substantial-equivalency individual. Practical answer matches the framed question. Dual-sourced: statute+rule + GA Board Statement of Policy No. 11.

physical_office_trigger.notes: GA office practicing public accounting or using CPA/CPA-firm titling requires licensure, untethered to service mix. Dual-sourced: statute + GA Board Statement of Policy No. 14 (offices register within 60 days of opening).

peer_review_conditions_permit.notes: Firms issuing attest/compilation reports must submit evidence of satisfactory peer review within 36 months preceding license expiration; noncompliant firms barred from licensure/renewal. Dual-sourced: statute+rule + GA Board Statement of Policy No. 20.
